title: Partial recursive functions: search and divergence

based_on.title: Computability and Incompleteness
based_on.pages: 9 (§1.2, partial functions); 33–35 (§2.5, strict partial operations, minimization and recursive functions; version 2007-01-09)

summary: Allow searches to run without a bound, keeping track of exactly when an output exists and when an earlier computation blocks the search.
abstract: Searching for a solution can return an answer, continue forever without finding one, or get stuck while testing a candidate. Partial functions describe this behavior by allowing some inputs to have no output. We extend primitive recursion with composition of partial functions and unbounded sequential search, obtaining the partial recursive functions. The search rule makes its order of evaluation explicit: a later successful candidate is reached only if every earlier test finishes. When each test terminates, the search returns the least solution whenever one exists; when every input has a solution, it defines a total recursive function. This separates the construction of a search procedure from a proof that it always terminates.
